chapters.title: Chapter 1: What TDS Is and How It Works

lessons.title: Tax at the Source: Why TDS Exists and How the Money Flows

body.text: TDS means the government collects tax at the moment income is paid, not months later when you file your return. The amount cut from your salary, interest or fees is not lost. It is an advance payment of your own tax, credited against your PAN.

children.text: Priya is a 27-year-old software engineer in Bengaluru earning ₹18,00,000 a year. She has never written a cheque to the Income Tax Department, yet by March she will have paid more than ₹1,50,000 in income tax. Her employer cuts about ₹12,567 from her salary every month. Her bank keeps back 10% of her fixed deposit interest. Dividends on the shares in her Zerodha account arrive 10% short once a company's payouts to her cross ₹10,000 in the year.

markDefs.definition: A system in which the person making certain payments withholds a portion as tax and deposits it with the government on behalf of the person receiving the money.

children.text: Every one of those cuts is
Tax Deducted at Source

, or TDS. It is the single biggest reason most Indians pay income tax without ever thinking about it. This lesson explains why the system exists and follows one rupee from the moment it is deducted to the moment it is counted against your final tax bill.
Why the Government Collects Tax at the Source

Imagine a system with no TDS. Every salaried employee, pensioner, freelancer and landlord receives the full amount, keeps it all year, and pays tax in one lump sum after the year ends. Three things go wrong.

cells: The government waits a whole year for its money and struggles to plan spending
Tax flows in every month as salaries, interest and fees are paid
Income that is never reported stays invisible
Every deduction creates a record linked to the PAN of the person receiving the money
Taxpayers face one large, painful payment and many simply cannot pay it
The burden is spread across the year in small pieces

body.title: Priya's year, with and without TDS

columns.label: Without TDS
points: Receives her full salary of ₹1,50,000 a month
Must set aside about ₹1,50,800 herself over the year
Pays it all at once after the year ends, with interest if she is late
The department only learns her income if she reports it

columns.label: With TDS
points: Receives about ₹1,37,433 a month after the tax cut, before other deductions like PF
Her employer deposits the tax with the government every month
By March, her tax for the year is already paid
Her income is on record with the department before she files anything

body.text: TDS is not an extra tax. It is your own income tax, collected early. If too much is deducted you get the excess back as a refund. If too little is deducted you pay the balance. Your final tax depends only on your total income for the year.

children.text: How the Money Flows: Four Steps

markDefs.definition: The person or organisation making the payment who is legally required to withhold tax from it, such as an employer, bank or company.
The person receiving the payment, from whose income the tax has been deducted. The TDS is credited against this person's PAN.

children.text: Every TDS transaction has two sides. The
deductor
is the one making the payment and holding back the tax. The
deductee
is the one receiving the money. Lesson 2 goes deeper into both roles. For now, follow the four steps.

cells: Withholds tax when the payment is made or credited, whichever happens first
At the time of payment or credit
Pays the deducted tax to the government
By the 7th of the next month (30 April for tax deducted in March)
Files a quarterly TDS statement listing every deductee's PAN and the tax deducted
Quarterly, for example 31 July for April to June
Sees the credit in Form 26AS (now Form 168) and AIS and subtracts it from final tax in the income tax return
When filing the return for that tax year

children.text: Steps 1 to 3 are the deductor's job, and the penalties for getting them wrong fall on the deductor. Step 4 is yours. Notice that you only get credit if the deductor has deposited the money and reported it against the correct PAN. That dependency is why checking your statement matters, and Chapter 5 is devoted to it.

body.title: Following one ₹1,00,000 invoice through the system

events.title: Invoice paid
events.description: Ananya, a freelance designer in Pune, bills a Mumbai ad agency ₹1,00,000 for a campaign. The agency deducts 10% TDS on professional fees, which is ₹10,000, and transfers ₹90,000 to her account.

events.title: Tax deposited
events.description: The agency pays the ₹10,000 to the government, quoting its own tax deduction account number (TAN).

events.title: Quarterly statement filed
events.description: The agency files its TDS statement for April to June 2026, reporting ₹10,000 against Ananya's PAN.

events.title: Credit visible
events.description: Once the statement is processed, the credit appears in Ananya's Form 26AS and AIS on the e-filing portal.

events.title: Credit claimed
events.description: Ananya files her return for tax year 2026-27, shows ₹1,00,000 as income and claims the ₹10,000 as tax already paid.

body.title: Quick Check: What Did Ananya Earn?
body.question: Ananya received ₹90,000 in her bank account for the ₹1,00,000 invoice. What income does she report in her tax return for this job?
options: Nothing, because tax has already been deducted
body.explanation: She reports the gross amount of ₹1,00,000, because that is what she earned. The ₹10,000 was her own tax, paid early on her behalf. She then claims that ₹10,000 as a credit. Reporting only ₹90,000 understates income, and it is one of the most common mismatches the department flags.

body.title: Why "payment or credit, whichever is earlier" matters

children.text: Businesses often record an expense in their books before they actually pay it. Say a Chennai company receives a ₹2,00,000 consulting bill on 28 March 2026, books it as payable on 31 March, and pays the consultant on 20 April.

The credit to the consultant's account in the books on 31 March comes first, so TDS must be deducted on that date, not on 20 April. That also means the March deadline of 30 April applies. And because the credit fell on or before 31 March 2026, the old Income-tax Act, 1961 governs this deduction, while a bill both booked and paid after 1 April 2026 falls under the new Act.
TDS Is a Credit, Not the Final Bill

markDefs.definition: The 12-month period from 1 April to 31 March for which income is taxed. The Income-tax Act, 2025 uses this single term in place of the old "previous year" and "assessment year".

children.text: Once your
tax year
ends, you add up all your income, work out the tax on it under your chosen regime, and subtract everything already paid. TDS is the largest of those payments for most people.

body.latex: \text{Balance payable or refund} = \text{Total tax on total income} - \text{TDS} - \text{TCS} - \text{Advance tax}
body.caption: A positive result is tax you still owe. A negative result is a refund due to you.

cells: Meera, homemaker with FD savings, Kochi

children.text: Rahul had rental income from a flat and capital gains on shares on top of his salary, and nobody deducted tax on those. Meera's total income was well below the level at which any tax is payable, yet her bank still deducted 10% on ₹60,000 of FD interest because it crossed the ₹50,000 threshold. TDS is a blunt tool. It applies to the payment, not to your whole financial picture.

body.title: Try It: Balance Tax or Refund?
body.prompt: Karthik, a bank officer in Chennai, works out his total tax for tax year 2026-27 as ₹84,500. His employer deducted ₹72,000 as TDS on salary and his bank deducted ₹6,200 on FD interest. He paid no advance tax. How much must he still pay? (Enter a negative number if he gets a refund.)
body.explanation: Total TDS is ₹72,000 + ₹6,200 = ₹78,200. Balance payable is ₹84,500 minus ₹78,200, which is ₹6,300. He pays it as self-assessment tax before filing his return.

body.text: A refund is not a bonus. It is your own money that sat with the government for a year or more. And a credit only reaches you if the deductor deposited the tax and reported it against the right PAN. A wrong digit in your PAN on the deductor's side can make a genuine deduction vanish from your statement.

children.text: Where You Meet TDS in Everyday Life

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, which applies to payments made or credited from 1 April 2026, TDS on salary sits in Section 392 (formerly Section 192). TDS on almost every other payment is consolidated into Section 393 (replacing the old Sections 193 to 194T and Section 195), organised as tables of payment types, rates and thresholds. Lesson 3 of this chapter walks through that change. The table below shows the payments you are most likely to meet.

body.caption: Common TDS situations for individuals (tax year 2026-27)

cells: Your average slab rate for the year
Estimated tax for the year is more than nil (Section 392, formerly 192)
Interest on bank FDs and RDs
Interest from that bank exceeds ₹50,000 in the year (₹1,00,000 for senior citizens)
Dividends from that company exceed ₹10,000 in the year
Businesses and professionals liable to deduct
Payments to you exceed ₹50,000 in the year
Rent paid by individuals not covered by tax audit

children.text: Chapter 2 is all about salary. Chapter 3 takes the other rows one by one, including crypto and online gaming, which follow their own rules.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Deposit Deadline
body.textWithBlank: Tax deducted by a private company from a vendor payment in August must be deposited with the government by ___ September.
body.explanation: For non-government deductors, TDS must be deposited by the 7th of the month after the deduction. The only exception is tax deducted in March, which can be deposited by 30 April.

stats.label: Deposit deadline
stats.context: Of the month after deduction. 30 April for March deductions

stats.label: TDS statements a year
stats.context: One per quarter, filed by the deductor

stats.label: Interest on late deduction
stats.context: Charged to the deductor. Section 398, formerly 201(1A)

stats.label: Interest on late deposit
stats.context: From date of deduction to date of deposit. Also charged to the deductor

body.title: Scenario: The Retired Teacher and Her Fixed Deposit
body.scenario: Neha is 64 and a retired school teacher in Jaipur. Her only income this tax year is ₹1,20,000 of interest on fixed deposits with SBI. Her total income is far below the level at which any tax is payable. In March, she notices SBI has deducted TDS.
body.prompt: How much TDS has SBI deducted, why did it deduct anything when she owes no tax, and what can she do about it now and next year?
body.modelAnswer: As a senior citizen, Neha's TDS threshold on bank interest is ₹1,00,000 a year. Her interest of ₹1,20,000 crosses it, so SBI deducts 10% on the entire amount, not just the excess: ₹12,000. The bank has no way of knowing her total tax is nil, because TDS looks at the payment, not the person's full income. This year she can file an income tax return and claim the full ₹12,000 back as a refund. Next year she can prevent the deduction altogether by giving SBI a self-declaration at the start of the year stating her tax liability is nil. This was Form 15H under the old rules and is now part of Form 121. Chapter 4 covers exactly how.

body.label: Extra tax TDS adds to your bill
body.context: TDS changes when you pay, never how much you owe. Your final tax is set by your total income and regime.

children.text: See Your Own TDS Trail

body.title: Find Every Deduction Made Against Your PAN
steps: Open your latest payslip and find the line labelled Income Tax or TDS. Note the amount
In your bank's net banking, download the TDS certificate or interest certificate for your fixed deposits
Log in to the income tax e-filing portal with your PAN and open the Annual Information Statement (AIS)
In the TDS/TCS section, list every deductor name you see: your employer, your bank, any company that paid you dividends
Check whether each amount in AIS matches your payslip and bank certificate. Note any gap to investigate after Chapter 5

body.label: Income Tax e-Filing Portal
body.description: Log in with your PAN to view Form 26AS and your Annual Information Statement, which list every TDS credit reported against you.

cards.definition: Tax Deducted at Source. The payer withholds part of certain payments and deposits it with the government against the receiver's PAN.
The person or organisation making the payment and deducting the tax, such as an employer, bank or company.
The person receiving the payment. The deducted tax is credited to this person.
Tax deducted and deposited on your behalf, which you subtract from your total tax when filing your return.
The 1 April to 31 March period for which income is taxed, the single term used by the Income-tax Act, 2025.
The section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 that consolidates TDS on non-salary payments, replacing the old Sections 193 to 194T and Section 195.
The tax credit statement showing TDS, TCS and tax paid against your PAN. Renumbered Form 168 under the Income-tax Rules, 2026.

points: TDS collects income tax at the moment certain payments are made, so tax reaches the government through the year instead of in one lump sum
It is a prepayment of your own tax, not an additional tax. Excess TDS comes back as a refund and a shortfall is paid as self-assessment tax
The deductor deducts, deposits by the 7th of the next month and reports quarterly. You claim the credit in your return
You only get credit if the deductor deposits the tax and reports it against your correct PAN, so checking Form 26AS and AIS matters
Always report the gross income, not the amount received after TDS, and then claim the TDS as a credit
From 1 April 2026, TDS on salary sits in Section 392 and TDS on most other payments in Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025
